To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel cache coherence scheme, DiCo-CM P, is proposed that achieves significant improvements in execution time and power consumption compared to a directory and a broadcast protocol.

a novel cache coherence scheme, DiCo-Cmp, achieves performance improvements of up to 7% over a directory protocol and up to 41% less traffic in the network compared to a token protocol, in tiled CMP architectures.

DiCo-CMP is a cache coherence protocol for tiled CMPs that: 1) reduces the miss latency of a directory protocol by 10-15%, 2) reduces the network traffic of a Token-CMP by 30-40%, and 3) reduces the power consumption of the interconnection network by 30-50% (all results are average values over a set of benchmarks).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient cache coherence protocols that will allow future CMP architectures to scale up to tens of cores.
the development of cache coherence protocols that are efficient in terms of performance and power, and are suited for future tiled CMP architectures.
the design of efficient cache coherence protocols for future CMP architectures, and DiCo-CMP is a first step in that direction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DiCo-CM P is a very good alternative to directory-based protocols in future tiled CMP architectures, and a very good alternative (or complement) to brute-force methods in terms of performance.
DiCo-Cmp achieves a better performance than Token-CMP while using less network resources.
our proposed DiCo-CMP cache coherence protocol is an efficient solution for future tiled CMP architectures, and that it can be used as an alternative to directory-based protocols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DiCo-Cmp achieves a 10% improvement on average over a state-of-the-art directory protocol and a 30% improvement on average compared to state-of-the-art broadcast protocols.
DiCo- CMP is a scalable, efficient, low-power cache coherence protocol that is specially suited to future CMP architectures.

DiCo-Cmp achieves a 10% reduction of execution time and 30% of network traffic on average over the best known directory protocol and the best known brute-force protocol, respectively, while it is as scalable as a brute-force protocol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design space of cache coherency protocols for future CMPs is much richer than the one that has been explored in the past.

, by exploiting the characteristics of tiled CMP architectures, it is possible to design cache coherence protocols with performance and network traffic characteristics that are closer to those of brute-force protocols, while maintaining the scalability and power efficiency of a directory protocol.
, in future tiled CMP architectures, the cache that must deliver a block can be the best place to maintain up-to-date information on sharing for that block.
